reason: All three attempts timed out on successive bug layers (root cause -> airless-disc fix -> live e2e failure -> gravity + friction bugs -> flaky canvas check), each of which is now resolved and committed (b345c9d, 0d667a3, 9a045f2; working tree clean, code verified matching the handoff). What remains is purely mechanical and fully specified in the handoff's ordered 'Next steps': (1) full unit suite ~2.5 min, (2) one more planet-approach e2e pass until it lands an airless home (~55%/run, so 1-3 runs x ~45 s), (3) the 7-spec e2e regression set on a single worker (~2-3 min; 6-8 spec sets historically run 1.3-1.6 min), (4) the fix(TASK-87) commit, (5) close-out (flip the 4 spec steps + board passes, LOG.md entry, delete handoff). That is ~15-25 min of a 45 min iteration, with the only bounded risks being the two documented flake families (wall-clock asserts, in-batch e2e load flakes), both of which resolve in 1-2 min isolated re-runs. Splitting would not help: the dominant cost is test execution, which a split task would repeat unchanged while paying a full fresh-session start, and a verify/close-out split would add a degenerate close-out-only task with no net time saved. Retry TASK-87 once as-is from its handoff.
